findings.title: 正文和表格的数对不上
findings.quote: 深度学习模型的 AUC 为 0.868, 显著优于 CURB-65 评分。
findings.context: 深度学习模型的 AUC 为 0.868, 显著优于 CURB-65 评分。年龄每增加 10 岁, 重症风险增加(OR = 1.45, 95%CI 1.12–1.88, P = 0.21)。
findings.evidence: The text gives 0.868 for '深度学习模型', but no cell of its table row matches at that precision; the nearest row value is 0.873.
findings.fix: Make the prose and the table report the same value, or name the derivation.

findings.title: 相对变化和它自己给的两个数对不上
findings.quote: 模型的 AUC 为 0.873, 较传统 CURB-65 评分(AUC 0.712)提高了 18.4%。
findings.context: 本研究纳入 2019 年至 2023 年某三甲医院收治的 412 例社区获得性肺炎患者, 构建深度学习模型预测 28 天内转入重症监护病房的风险。模型的 AUC 为 0.873, 较传统 CURB-65 评分(AUC 0.712)提高了 18.4%。
findings.evidence: The sentence gives a 18.4% change of 0.873 over 0.712, but relative to 0.712 those numbers give 22.6%.
findings.fix: Recompute the percentage from 0.873 and 0.712 and correct it wherever it is quoted.

findings.title: 百分比和计数对不上
findings.quote: 412例中有 98 例(25.8%)在 28 天内转入重症监护病房。
findings.context: 共纳入 412 例患者, 其中男性 236 例(57.3%), 女性 176 例(42.7%)。412例中有 98 例(25.8%)在 28 天内转入重症监护病房。
findings.fix: Correct the percentage to 23.8%, or the count or denominator if one of those is the typo.

findings.title: p 值和检验统计量算不回来
findings.context: 重症组患者年龄显著高于非重症组(71.2 ± 9.8 岁 vs 63.5 ± 12.1 岁, t = 1.21, P = 0.002)。两组吸烟史比例差异无统计学意义(χ²(1) = 2.85, P = 0.091)。
findings.evidence: t = 1.21 cannot give p = 0.002: whatever the degrees of freedom, its two-sided p is at least .224. The result is not significant at 0.05.
findings.fix: Recompute p from t and its degrees of freedom, and report the degrees of freedom.

findings.title: 置信区间和 p 值互相矛盾
findings.context: 深度学习模型的 AUC 为 0.868, 显著优于 CURB-65 评分。年龄每增加 10 岁, 重症风险增加(OR = 1.45, 95%CI 1.12–1.88, P = 0.21)。
findings.evidence: The interval 1.12 to 1.88 excludes the null value 1, but p = 0.21 says the opposite at 0.05. A 95% interval and a two-sided p from the same estimate agree on significance.
findings.fix: Recheck the interval and the p-value against the analysis output and correct the one that is wrong; if they come from different models, say so.

matched.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Adults with Community-acquired Pneumonia. An Official Clinical Practice Guideline of the American Thoracic Society and Infectious Diseases Society of America

items.abstract: Abstract Background This document provides evidence-based clinical practice guidelines on the management of adult patients with community-acquired pneumonia. Methods A multidisciplinary panel conducted pragmatic systematic reviews of the relevant research and applied Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation methodology for clinical recommendations. Results The panel addressed 16 specific areas for recommendations spanning questions of diagnostic testing, determination of site of care, selection of initial empiric antibiotic therapy, and subsequent management decisions. Although some recommendations remain unchanged from the 2007 guideline, the availability of results from new therapeutic trials and epidemiological investigations led to revised recommendations for empiric treatment strategies and additional management decisions. Conclusions The panel formulated and provided the rationale for recommendations on selected diagnostic and treatment strategies for adult patients with community-acquired pneumonia.

items.abstract: BACKGROUND: In the assessment of severity in community acquired pneumonia (CAP), the modified British Thoracic Society (mBTS) rule identifies patients with severe pneumonia but not patients who might be suitable for home management. A multicentre study was conducted to derive and validate a practical severity assessment model for stratifying adults hospitalised with CAP into different management groups. METHODS: Data from three prospective studies of CAP conducted in the UK, New Zealand, and the Netherlands were combined. A derivation cohort comprising 80% of the data was used to develop the model. Prognostic variables were identified using multiple logistic regression with 30 day mortality as the outcome measure. The final model was tested against the validation cohort. RESULTS: 1068 patients were studied (mean age 64 years, 51.5% male, 30 day mortality 9%). items.reference: [5] Lundberg SM, Lee SI. A unified approach to interpreting model predictions. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems. 2017;30.

matched.title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions

items.abstract: Understanding why a model makes a certain prediction can be as crucial as the prediction's accuracy in many applications. However, the highest accuracy for large modern datasets is often achieved by complex models that even experts struggle to interpret, such as ensemble or deep learning models, creating a tension between accuracy and interpretability. In response, various methods have recently been proposed to help users interpret the predictions of complex models, but it is often unclear how these methods are related and when one method is preferable over another. To address this problem, we present a unified framework for interpreting predictions, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations). SHAP assigns each feature an importance value for a particular prediction. Its novel components include: (1) the identification of a new class of additive feature importance measures, and (2) theoretical results showing there is a unique solution in this class with a set of desirable properties. The new class unifies six existing methods, notable because several recent methods in the class lack the proposed desirable properties. Based on insights from this unification, we present new methods that show improved computational performance and/or better consistency with human intuition than previous approaches.
